title: Deconstructing The Ethics of Large Language Models from Long-standing Issues to New-emerging Dilemmas: A Survey

bias_targets.methodology: As a survey paper, it categorizes and reviews existing methodologies for measuring social bias in LLMs into three main types: embedding-based metrics (calculating distances between neutral and identity-specific terms), probability-based metrics (comparing token prediction probabilities for different social groups), and generated text-based metrics (evaluating frequency distributions, using auxiliary classifiers, and applying lexicon-based scores).

The paper reviews existing literature that measures gender bias by calculating distances within the embedding space between neutral terms (e.g., job titles) and identity-specific terms (e.g., gender pronouns).

The paper discusses racial bias in the context of literature that reviews standalone networks and intra-processing mitigation strategies designed specifically to measure and reduce racial stereotyping in model outputs.
